issues.source_quote: Фрис-стрит, рыбна улица, - Аптека «Чиканук»...
issues.translation_quote: Fries Street, Fish Street, - The "Chikanuk" pharmacy...
issues.justification: The mangled pseudo-foreign street name (Фрис-стрит, рыбна улица) is a coded phrase that the speaker is rehearsing. 'Fries Street' mistranslates it, and the broken, accented quality of the Russian is lost.

issues.source_quote: Пора, турыст! Нынадо... Иди...
issues.translation_quote: Time to go, tooreest! Don'... Go on...
issues.justification: 'Нынадо' is a slurred 'Не надо' said in Lyolik's mock-foreign voice. The English 'Don'...' loses that meaning and reads as a truncation.

issues.source_quote: Кон-тра-бан-да!
issues.translation_quote: Nothing special - ordinary contraband... - What? - Con-tra-band!
issues.justification: The captain's calm line is rendered correctly, but the surrounding exchange loses the sense that Semyon is thunderstruck. The comic understatement is weakened by the flat 'What?'.

issues.source_quote: Ай-й... Спасибо Вам большое, Вы уж меня извините что я…
issues.translation_quote: Ow... Thank you so much, and please forgive me for...
issues.justification: The exchange is slightly garbled. The line is not as natural as it could be in English, and the cast-on-arm gag is lost in 'Ow...'.

issues.source_quote: Нет, на это я пойтить не могу!
issues.translation_quote: No, I ain't goin' along with that!
issues.justification: Lyolik is a thug posing as a policeman, not an uneducated rustic. The deliberately substandard 'пойтить' is mimicked by heavy dialect ('ain't goin'') that overshoots the character's register and clashes with his otherwise polished speech.

issues.source_quote: Не виноватая я! Он сам пришёл!
issues.translation_quote: I ain't the guilty one! He come here by himself!
issues.justification: The Russian is a simple colloquial protest. The invented non-standard English dialect makes the character sound like a different type of speaker and creates a comic effect absent from the original.

issues.source_quote: Собака - друг человека! ... Управдом - друг человека!
issues.translation_quote: the building manager is man's best friend!
issues.justification: 'Управдом' (house manager) is a satirical Soviet type; 'building manager' is acceptable, but 'best friend' changes the formula 'друг человека' (a friend of man) and the humor of the reversal is blunted.

issues.source_quote: Куй железо, не отходя от кассы!
issues.translation_quote: strike while the iron's... at the cash register!
issues.justification: The intentionally mangled proverb (a blend of 'strike while the iron is hot' and 'не отходя от кассы') is a signature catchphrase of the chief. The English rendering, with the awkward '...' break, is repeated inconsistently and the blend comes across as clumsy rather than as a witty malapropism.

issues.source_quote: Кто возьмёт билетов пачку, тот получит... Водокачку!
issues.translation_quote: Whoever buys a stack of tickets wins... A smokestack!
issues.justification: The rhymed jingle (пачку/водокачку) is a joke on a prize that is a water tower. 'Smokestack' changes the referent and loses the absurd rhymed slogan; it does not rhyme in English.

issues.source_quote: за чужой счёт пьют даже трезвенники и язвенники
issues.translation_quote: even ascetics drink... and diabetics
issues.justification: 'Язвенники' means people with stomach ulcers, not diabetics. 'Ascetics' is also a poor fit for 'трезвенники' (teetotalers). This is a mistranslation that weakens the aphorism.

issues.source_quote: Строго на север, порядка... 50-ти метров, расположен туалэт, типа сортир, обозначенный на схеме буквами «Мэ» и «Жо».
issues.translation_quote: Due north, approximately... 50 meters, there is located a toilette, type: latrine, marked on the diagram with the letters "M" and "Zh".
issues.justification: The joke is that the letters М and Ж (men/women) are pronounced in a vulgar way as 'Мэ' and 'Жо' (the latter sounding like 'жопа'). The English loses the wordplay entirely.

issues.source_quote: пыхты
issues.translation_quote: the fyr tree
issues.justification: The spelling 'fyr' imitates a mispronunciation not present in the way the Russian is written (пыхта for пихта), and the translation then switches to 'fir tree', which is inconsistent.

issues.source_quote: Ум-м... Феденька... и хорошо бы... дичь.
issues.translation_quote: Fedya, dear... and some... game would be nice.
issues.justification: The key running gag is that 'дичь' means both 'game' (food) and the code name for the operation/victim. This is lost in places, and the later 'под дичь водку не пьют' joke becomes confusing.

issues.source_quote: Вылитый Володька Трынкин!
issues.translation_quote: the spitting image of Volodka Trynkin!
issues.justification: The surname 'Трынкин' echoes 'трын-трава' from the song of the hares and is a deliberate comic name. The pun is not carried across.

issues.source_quote: трынь-траву
issues.translation_quote: never-mind weed
issues.justification: 'Трын-трава' is an idiom meaning 'nothing matters / don't care'. Rendering it as 'never-mind weed' is a calque that works only partly, and 'Which is also a plant' is lost. It also appears inconsistently.

issues.source_quote: Чтоб ты жил на одну зарплату!
issues.translation_quote: May you live on just your salary!
issues.justification: Part of the humor is that this is the neighbor's comedic curse. The English is fine but the curse chain is less punchy than the original.

issues.source_quote: Шампанское по утрам пьют или аристократы, или дегенераты!
issues.translation_quote: Only two kinds drink champagne in the morning: aristocrats and degenerates!
issues.justification: This is a famous quote and the English is acceptable, but the order-of-words punch is weaker than the original rhythm.

issues.source_quote: В измене!
issues.translation_quote: To treason!
issues.justification: In context Nadya means marital infidelity ('измена' also means adultery), and the comic misunderstanding is that she suspects an affair or treason. 'Treason' alone drops the double meaning.

issues.source_quote: Ксива? Паспорт... готов! Хаза? Отель «Атлантик».
issues.translation_quote: Papers? The passport... is ready! Crib? The Hotel Atlantic.
issues.justification: The criminal slang ('ксива', 'хаза') is a parodic jargon. 'Crib' is modern American slang that is anachronistic for a 1969 Soviet film and clashes with the register.

issues.source_quote: Лопух... Такого возьмём без шума и пыли!
issues.translation_quote: A sucker... We'll take him with no fuss, no dust!
issues.justification: 'Без шума и пыли' is an idiom ('quietly, without fuss'). Translating 'пыли' literally as 'dust' sounds odd, and 'no fuss, no dust' is used repeatedly as a catchphrase but is unnatural.

issues.source_quote: Не взял попутных - это не таксист!
issues.translation_quote: Won't pick up passengers - he's no cabbie!
issues.justification: The line indicates he did not pick up passers-by who were along the route; 'passengers' is imprecise and the reasoning is lost.

issues.source_quote: Ну что Вы, время! Время - деньги!
issues.translation_quote: Come on, time! Time is money!
issues.justification: The line is literal and slightly clumsy.

issues.source_quote: Упал, выругался... Чёрт возьми! Ух, прости, "Чёрт побери!"
issues.translation_quote: "Dammit!" Oops, sorry, "Damn it all!"
issues.justification: The password 'Чёрт побери' is a fixed phrase, and the difference between the two variants is the entire joke. The English 'Dammit' vs. 'Damn it all' is too weak a distinction, and the later 'Dyamn' spellings are inconsistent.

issues.source_quote: Пурген ласт "Чёрт побери"?
issues.translation_quote: Dyamn it all...
issues.justification: The mispronounced password ('Щёрт побери') is rendered with ad hoc spellings ('Dyamn', 'tsdyamn') that are unrelated to the sound-based gag in Russian and vary erratically.

issues.source_quote: Вы в самодеятельности участвуете?
issues.translation_quote: Do you do amateur theater?
issues.justification: Soviet 'самодеятельность' is amateur arts/talent circles; 'amateur theater' narrows it. The later 'no amateur theatrics' translating 'без самодеятельности' (no improvising) changes the meaning.

issues.source_quote: Сеня, давай махнём на рыбалку а?
issues.translation_quote: Senya, let's go fishing, huh?
issues.justification: Acceptable but the colloquial Russian 'махнём' has more energy than the English.

issues.source_quote: Новыми?
issues.translation_quote: New rubles?
issues.justification: The reference is to the 1961 currency reform (new vs. old money); this is rendered literally without clarity for English readers.

issues.source_quote: Простите, маленькая техническая неувязка...
issues.translation_quote: Excuse us, a slight technical hitch...
issues.justification: Acceptable, but the fashion-show parody of a bureaucratic announcer register is flattened elsewhere ('Honorable mention', 'Design team').

issues.source_quote: Рогаль Левицкая
issues.translation_quote: Rogal-Levitskaya
issues.justification: Inconsistent transliteration of a name that is presumably a joke on a pastry/croissant ('рогалик').

issues.source_quote: Господу помолимся...
issues.translation_quote: Let us pray to the Lord...
issues.justification: The Church Slavonic archaic register is rendered into plain English, with only 'unto ages of ages' echoing the original archaism.

issues.source_quote: Такова «сё ля ви», как говорят у них...
issues.translation_quote: "C'est la vie", as they say over here...
issues.justification: The speaker refers to foreigners' expression ('у них' = over there, abroad). 'Over here' reverses the meaning.

issues.source_quote: Ты ушёл бы от такой женщины?
issues.translation_quote: Gesha, would you leave a woman like that?
issues.justification: Acceptable; the comic cadence is slightly flat.

issues.source_quote: Где телефон?
issues.translation_quote: This is Semyon Semyonovich Gorbunkov. ... Send a taxi to the "Weeping Willow" restaurant.
issues.justification: The call to the 'taxi' is the agreed signal for the police, and the message is fine, but later 'Hotel Atlantic' vs 'Atlantica' is inconsistent in the translation.

issues.source_quote: Во!... Ясно...
issues.translation_quote: Wow!... I see...
issues.justification: 'Во!' is a gesture accompanying a verbal description of the woman. 'Wow!' is a loose rendering of a gesture-word.

issues.source_quote: Пятый, пятый, он вошёл, приём!
issues.translation_quote: Five, Five, he's gone in, over!
issues.justification: Consistent radio register, but 'Nine hundred hours' for 'девять ноль-ноль' is fine; no issue beyond minor over-formality.

issues.source_quote: Значит, этот лопух ничего не знает.
issues.translation_quote: So the sucker doesn't know a thing.
issues.justification: 'Лопух' (a naïve fool) is rendered as 'sucker', which suggests being cheated; acceptable, but the translator renders 'лопух' variously ('sucker', 'dummy'), losing consistency.

issues.source_quote: Геша, ты ушёл бы
issues.translation_quote: Gesha
issues.justification: Diminutive forms of names (Геша, Лёлик, Сеня) are retained, which is fine, but Kozladoyev/Kozadoyev wordplay (козёл) is lost, with 'Kozladoyev' offered without any cue to English readers.

issues.source_quote: Здорово у вас здесь всё оборудовано.
issues.translation_quote: Well, well... You've got it all nicely set up here.
issues.justification: Acceptable, but the English 'Well, well...' adds suspicion not present.

issues.source_quote: Я слишком много знал...
issues.translation_quote: I knew too much...
issues.justification: The deadpan joke ('as a dead acquaintance of mine used to say') works, but 'the late one' is awkward phrasing.

issues.source_quote: Ва-ба-ба-ба-пфа-ба-ва-бэдум
issues.translation_quote: Va-ba-ba-ba-pfa-ba-va-bedum
issues.justification: Nonsense scat is transliterated, fine, but 'Oh yes, bee chel, lurai... uye...' is an unexplained imitation of English; acceptable.
